technique: Dangling CNAME to a deprovisioned provider endpoint
signal: CNAME points to a provider host returning the provider's unclaimed-resource fingerprint (NoSuchBucket / no GitHub Pages site here / 404 from an unregistered app)
detect_cmd: dig +short CNAME HOST; curl -sSI https://HOST

signal: Anonymous ListBucket returns a key listing (200 + XML) rather than 403 AccessDenied
detect_cmd: curl -sS 'https://BUCKET.s3.amazonaws.com/?list-type=2'

signal: /.git/HEAD returns 'ref: refs/heads/...' with 200 and a non-HTML content-type
detect_cmd: curl -sS https://HOST/.git/HEAD

signal: /.env returns KEY=VALUE lines with 200 and a non-HTML content-type
detect_cmd: curl -sS https://HOST/.env

signal: An introspection query returns the full type system instead of an error
detect_cmd: curl -sS -X POST HOST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query":"{__schema{queryType{name}}}"}'

signal: A low-privilege account (yours) resolves a field or mutation intended for admins
detect_cmd: # with two accounts you own, request privileged fields as the low-priv one

signal: Response echoes an arbitrary Origin in ACAO and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
detect_cmd: curl -sSI -H 'Origin: https://evil.example' HOST

signal: An injected %0d%0a sequence produces a real, separate response header
detect_cmd: curl -sSI 'HOST?p=%0d%0aX-Injected:1'

signal: A 3xx Location header points to an attacker-controlled external origin
detect_cmd: curl -sSI 'HOST?next=https://evil.example'

technique: Server-side request forgery via URL parameter
signal: The server fetches an OAST URL you control (DNS or HTTP callback) from a param such as url=, dest=, image=
detect_cmd: curl -sS 'HOST?url=http://OAST_DOMAIN/'

technique: Object reference with no ownership check
signal: A second account you registered can read or modify an object id it does not own
detect_cmd: # requires two accounts you own; compare authz on the same object id

technique: JWT alg confusion / none / weak secret
signal: The server accepts alg:none, or an HS256 token signed with the public key or a guessable secret
detect_cmd: # decode the header; test alg:none acceptance against an endpoint you have an account on

signal: /swagger.json, /openapi.json or /api-docs returns a machine-readable API contract
detect_cmd: curl -sS HOST/openapi.json

signal: A VERIFIED live credential (not a publishable key) appears in a JS bundle
detect_cmd: # trufflehog --only-verified against the JS URL

signal: A nuclei template (not merely a version string) confirms the CVE is present
detect_cmd: nuclei -u HOST -tags cve -severity high,critical

signal: A zone delegates to a nameserver that is registrable at its provider
detect_cmd: dig NS DOMAIN; check registrability of each NS at its provider

signal: Appending a static-looking suffix to an authenticated URL causes private content to be cached and served to others
detect_cmd: # with a cache-buster, compare X-Cache HIT/MISS on a .css-suffixed private URL

technique: Host header poisons generated absolute URLs
signal: A reset link is generated using an attacker-supplied Host header
detect_cmd: # request a reset with Host: evil.example on an account you own; inspect the link

signal: /actuator/env or /actuator/heapdump returns 200 with sensitive data
detect_cmd: curl -sS HOST/actuator/env

signal: A directory URL returns an autogenerated 'Index of /' listing
detect_cmd: curl -sS HOST/uploads/

signal: A .js.map returns 200 with a valid source map ("version":3,"sources":[...]), exposing original source and often inline comments/secrets
detect_cmd: curl -sS HOST | head -c 120

signal: /.DS_Store returns 200 with macOS binary metadata (magic bytes Bud1) that parses into otherwise-hidden directory entries
detect_cmd: curl -sS HOST -o- | head -c 8 | xxd

signal: A backup or archive path (.sql/.bak/.zip/.tar.gz/.old/~) returns 200 with archive or source content instead of 404
detect_cmd: curl -sSI HOST

signal: A boolean/error/time payload changes the response versus a control (' vs '' , SLEEP(5) vs SLEEP(0))
detect_cmd: # sqlmap -u URL --batch --level 1 --risk 1 --technique=BEUST (detection only, no --dump/--os-shell)

signal: {{7*7}} / ${7*7} / #{7*7} evaluates to 49 while a control (${7*8}) does not
detect_cmd: # send {{7*7}} and ${7*7}; compare rendered output to a control

signal: An injected ; | or backtick command triggers an OAST callback or a measurable delay vs control
detect_cmd: # inject ;curl OAST_DOMAIN or |sleep 5; confirm callback or timing vs control

signal: A ../ payload reads a file outside webroot (etc/passwd, win.ini) or changes content vs a control path
detect_cmd: # compare ?file=../../../../etc/passwd against a control value

signal: An external entity in posted XML triggers an OAST callback or reflects file content
detect_cmd: # POST XML with a DOCTYPE SYSTEM entity to an OAST you control; confirm callback

signal: Operator injection ([$ne],[$gt]) alters auth/query results vs a control
detect_cmd: # send param[$ne]= vs param= and compare responses

signal: A serialized blob (rO0AB java / O: php / BAh ruby) in a param or cookie is trusted; a benign gadget reaches OAST
detect_cmd: # identify magic bytes; test a benign OAST gadget only, supervised

technique: Unrestricted file upload to code execution
signal: A dangerous-extension file is stored web-accessibly and executes at the returned URL
detect_cmd: # upload a benign marker with .php/.jsp extension; check if it renders/executes

signal: A unique marker reflects unencoded into an executable context while a control is encoded
detect_cmd: # dalfox url URL --only-poc (detection); confirm context + encoding vs control

signal: A source (location/hash/postMessage) flows to a sink (innerHTML/eval) and executes in-browser
detect_cmd: # browser client-probe: set the source, confirm sink execution

signal: __proto__/constructor keys pollute Object.prototype, changing behaviour or reaching a gadget
detect_cmd: # send __proto__[x]=y; check the property leaking into a response or behaviour

signal: A sensitive page loads in an iframe (no X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors)
detect_cmd: curl -sSI HOST | grep -iE 'x-frame-options|content-security-policy'

signal: redirect_uri accepts an attacker origin or state is missing/static, enabling token theft or login CSRF
detect_cmd: # vary redirect_uri to a controlled origin; observe whether the code/token is delivered there

signal: An assertion is accepted with a stripped/altered signature or XML signature wrapping
detect_cmd: # test signature-exclusion / XSW on an assertion for an account you own

signal: Host-header-poisoned reset link, predictable/non-expiring token, or reset that disables MFA
detect_cmd: # request reset with Host: evil on your own account; inspect the link + token lifecycle

signal: The session identifier is not rotated on authentication
detect_cmd: # compare the session cookie pre- and post-login on an account you own

signal: Duplicate/plus-addressed email accepted, a role field is honoured, or verification is not enforced
detect_cmd: # register with a role/admin field and with a duplicate/plus-addressed email

signal: A low-privilege account invokes an admin-only endpoint or HTTP verb
detect_cmd: # with two accounts you own, call privileged endpoints/verbs as the low-priv one

signal: An unexpected body field (role, is_admin, balance) is persisted
detect_cmd: # add role/is_admin to a create/update body on your own account; check persistence

signal: Deeply nested or aliased/batched queries are accepted without depth/complexity limits
detect_cmd: # send a modest nested/aliased query; confirm absence of depth limits (do NOT amplify)

signal: A WebSocket accepts cross-origin handshakes or lacks per-message authorization
detect_cmd: # handshake with a foreign Origin; check acceptance and per-message authz

technique: Race condition on a single-use resource
signal: Parallel requests use a single-use action more than once (coupon, withdrawal, vote)
detect_cmd: # send N parallel identical requests to a single-use action on your own account

signal: A CL.TE/TE.CL desync lets a crafted prefix affect a subsequent request
detect_cmd: # timing-based CL.TE/TE.CL probe with a buster ONLY, supervised, per the SKILL gate

signal: An unkeyed header (X-Forwarded-Host etc.) is reflected and cached, served to other users
detect_cmd: # with a cache-buster, test unkeyed-header reflection; never poison a shared cache key

signal: wpscan/nuclei confirms a vulnerable core, plugin, or theme version
detect_cmd: nuclei -u HOST -tags wordpress,wp-plugin -severity medium,high,critical

signal: An admin/management panel is internet-reachable (a candidate for default creds or a known CVE)
detect_cmd: nuclei -u HOST -tags panel,exposed-panel,default-login

signal: A default credential pair is accepted (nuclei default-logins, detection only)
detect_cmd: nuclei -u HOST -tags default-login
